repo: https://github.com/realiti4/claude-swap. Read-only study of main at commit 9aa6d02 (2026-09-20, pyproject version 0.27.0b1). The latest release is v0.26.0 (2026-09-02), which is also the PyPI version. The repo has about 2,860 stars and 310 forks, and 395 issues and PRs, all of which I read by title and the relevant ones in full. It was cloned for reading into the session scratchpad at .../scratchpad/claude-swap. cswap-desktop (TheSkinnyRat) was not studied in this task.
what_it_is:
A Python 3.12+ command-line tool (entry points cswap and claude-swap, both mapped to claude_swap.cli:main; dependencies textual, truststore, and keyring on Windows only) that manages several Claude Code logins for one person on one machine. It copies ~/.claude/.credentials.json (or the macOS Keychain item) and the oauthAccount block of ~/.claude.json in and out of per-account backup slots. It reads usage for every slot from Anthropic's OAuth usage endpoint and can switch the default login on a threshold or run an account in a single terminal through CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR ('session mode'). Surfaces: CLI, a Textual TUI, and a macOS menu bar. There is no server, no relay and no remote access of its own. The maintainer frames it as the same as doing /logout and /login by hand (issue #31).

What bears on Ashley:
(1) `cswap run` is almost exactly Ashley's model: one CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR per account. Its seeding recipe is directly reusable (details under the run feature).
(2) The usage endpoint does NOT work for setup-tokens. Details are under limit_detection; the practical upshot is that Ashley should read limits from its own `claude -p` output.
(3) Its lock protocol for Claude Code's own credential locks, and its note that fcntl.flock gives no exclusion across nodes on NFS (#372), matter on a grid where several nodes share one home directory.
(4) Remote Control ownership findings (#198, PR #210) explain why the Remote Control login must stay in a config directory that rotation never touches.

features.name: add: capture the currently logged-in account
features.how_it_works: Reads the live credential: ~/.claude/.credentials.json on Linux, WSL and Windows; the Keychain item 'Claude Code-credentials' on macOS (with a sha256(NFC(CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR))[:8] suffix when that variable is set); CLAUDE_SECURESTORAGE_CONFIG_DIR is honoured since #205. It also reads oauthAccount {emailAddress, accountUuid, organizationUuid, organizationName} from ~/.claude.json (or $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/.claude.json, or the legacy <config>/.config.json). Ownership is checked with GET https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/profile (Bearer access token, 5 s timeout), which returns account.uuid, email and organization.uuid (#216). Stored as <backup>/credentials/.creds-<N>-<email>.enc, which is base64 and NOT encrypted, mode 0600; plus <backup>/configs/.claude-config-<N>-<email>.json; plus the roster <backup>/sequence.json {activeAccountNumber, sequence[], accounts{N:{email, organizationUuid, organizationName, alias, disabled}}}. Options: --slot N, --alias. Re-running add after a re-login updates the slot in place. The README warns not to run /logout between logins, because current Claude Code may revoke the refresh token of the account being left (#189).

features.name: add-token: register a raw setup-token or API key without a browser login
features.how_it_works: `cswap add-token sk-ant-oat01-... [--slot N] [--email X]`; passing `-` reads the token from stdin, and an empty value prompts with getpass. A setup-token is wrapped as {"claudeAiOauth":{"accessToken":<token>,"scopes":["user:inference"]}}, with no refreshToken and no expiresAt; SETUP_TOKEN_SCOPES in switcher.py:106 carries the comment 'Matches Claude Code's CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN path'. Without --email the placeholder is setup-token-<slot>@token.local. A value starting sk-ant-api is stored raw as a managed API-key account. No Anthropic API calls are made. It exists for headless servers (#24).

features.name: switch: change the default login in place
features.how_it_works: `cswap switch` rotates to the next account; `cswap switch N|email|alias` picks one; `--strategy best|next-available` picks by usage; `--force` re-activates after an import. _perform_switch first resolves the live credential's owner outside all locks: it compares the SHA-256 fingerprint of the refresh token, and if that does not settle it, calls /api/oauth/profile. It then holds three locks, taken in this order: its own FileLock(<backup>/.lock); Claude Code's credential locks; and Claude Code's config lock. Under those locks it: (a) backs up the outgoing live credential after classifying it as own-bytes, own-family, own-rotated or foreign; (b) writes the target credential atomically with mkstemp and os.replace, then chmod 0600; (c) writes the target's oauthAccount into ~/.claude.json. Machine-shared keys (mcpOAuth, mcpOAuthClientConfig, mcpXaaIdp, mcpXaaIdpConfig, pluginSecrets) are kept from the live copy; trustedDeviceToken stays with its slot. Only one auth method is left active: activating OAuth clears primaryApiKey, and activating an API key clears the OAuth credential. No restart is needed: Claude Code drops its cached token when .credentials.json's mtime changes, so on Linux and Windows the switch applies on the next message. On macOS the Keychain cache takes about 30 s, and cswap rewrites an existing .credentials.json to bump its mtime (#86).

features.name: Cooperating with Claude Code's own locks
features.how_it_works: Reimplements the npm proper-lockfile protocol, verified by the author against the 2.1.218 bundle, where the lock is a directory and mkdir's atomicity is the mutex. The credential locks are <config-home>/.oauth_refresh.lock, then the legacy ~/.claude.lock (<config-home>.lock), taken in Claude Code's order; they count as stale after 60 s and live holders touch them every 5 s. The config lock ~/.claude.json.lock counts as stale after 10 s. cswap touches every 3 s and waits at most 9 s per lock, with no network calls while any lock is held. Holding these locks means a swap can never land inside Claude Code's read, refresh, save sequence. Separately, FileLock (fcntl.flock on POSIX, msvcrt on Windows) guards cswap's own files. Issue #372 measured 2,653 exclusion failures in 2,829 acquisitions across two nodes sharing an NFS home mounted local_lock=all, against 0 with mkdir. The mkdir fix is PR #374, not yet merged.

features.name: list / status: usage dashboard and JSON
features.how_it_works: GET https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/usage with headers 'Authorization: Bearer <access token>', 'anthropic-beta: oauth-2025-04-20' and 'User-Agent: claude-swap/1.0'. The response is normalised as described under limit_detection. `--json` emits schemaVersion 1 with activeAccountNumber and accounts[]. Each account carries number, email, active, usageStatus and usage {fiveHour|sevenDay:{pct, resetsAt}}, plus usageFetchedAt, usageAgeSeconds, lastGoodUsage, usageError (e.g. http-429, timeout), usageRetryAt, loginExpiresAt (from refreshTokenExpiresAt), alias and disabled. Weekly windows also carry expectedPct, aheadOfPace, projectedExhaustionAt and willLastToReset. `--token-status` prints the expiry and refresh-token state of each stored credential.
features.source: src/claude_swap/oauth.py (request_usage_data, build_usage_result), src/claude_swap/json_output.py, src/claude_swap/pace.py, README 'JSON output for scripting'

features.name: Shared usage cache and polling cadence
features.how_it_works: <backup>/cache holds a per-account table that every surface shares: the last good reading, failure and backoff state, and nextPollAt. A collector claims accounts (claimUntil, 90 s lease) under FileLock, fetches with no lock held, then merges under the lock. When a fetch fails, the last good numbers are kept. Cadence constants (in poll_policy.py): SERVE_TTL 180 s; MIN_INTERVAL 180 s; URGENT 60 s, used only when the active account is near the threshold and moving; ACTIVE_MAX 300 s; CANDIDATE up to 600 s; EXHAUSTED 600 s. The author measured the endpoint's budget at about 28-30 requests per rolling hour per identity × user-agent class, and in one regime the budget is per account rather than per token. A 429 with Retry-After: 0 triggers a 300 s edge backoff and a 360 s floor for an hour; repeated 429s back off multiplicatively (×1.5, up to 1,800 s). Requests are jittered ±10% and staggered 0.25 s.

features.name: auto: switch before the limit
features.how_it_works: `cswap auto` runs a foreground loop that polls every 60 s. When the active account's binding window, max(5h%, 7d%, plus the per-model weekly windows named by --model/autoswitch.model), reaches the threshold (default 90), it switches to the candidate with the most headroom. That candidate must be below the threshold and at least hysteresisPct (10) points better; cooldownSeconds (300) is ignored when the account is hard at its limit. Strategies are best and consume-first (spend the account whose weekly window resets soonest). Before activating a target it refreshes the target's token if it expires within 10 minutes (FRESHEN_BUFFER_MS), and quarantines targets whose refresh fails with invalid_grant. After unhealthyTicks (3) failed reads it fails over. Options: --once (exit codes 0 switched, 1 error, 2 nothing to do, 3 blocked), --dry-run, and --json, which emits JSON lines of kinds poll, switch, no-switch, account-quarantined, all-exhausted and error. State is kept in <backup>/autoswitch_state.json. API-key accounts are excluded unless --include-api-key-accounts is passed.

features.name: Refresh-token gate (refresh tokens are single-use)
features.how_it_works: Refreshes only inactive slots, with POST https://platform.claude.com/v1/oauth/token {grant_type: refresh_token, refresh_token, client_id: 9d1c250a-e61b-44d9-88ed-5944d1962f5e}. The response supplies access_token, expires_in, refresh_token, scope and optionally account/organization. The active account is never refreshed, because Claude Code owns it. consume_backup_grant takes a per-slot lock <backup>/credentials/.consume-<N>.lock, re-reads the newest copy, POSTs, then saves only if the refresh-token fingerprint is unchanged (compare-and-swap). If that save fails, the new token is stashed as .unclaimed-<id>.enc (`cswap unclaimed` lists these). invalid_grant or invalid_client in a 400/401/403 body means the lineage is dead. #381 and #164 show that presenting a superseded refresh token, or refreshing a copy that another location also holds, revokes the other holder's access token immediately.

features.name: run: session mode, one account per terminal
features.how_it_works: `cswap run N [-- claude args]` execs claude with CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=<backup>/sessions/<N>-<email-slug>. It first strips ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN, CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN_FILE_DESCRIPTOR and CLAUDE_CODE_API_KEY_FILE_DESCRIPTOR from the environment. Seeding: .credentials.json (0600), and .claude.json merged with {oauthAccount, hasCompletedOnboarding: true, theme}; the theme key is required, otherwise onboarding appears. Validation: `claude auth status --json` must give loggedIn true, authMethod 'claude.ai', a matching email, and orgId if present; a 10 s timeout counts as 'unknown', not 'invalid'. Sharing: settings.json, keybindings.json, CLAUDE.md, skills, commands and agents are symlinked on POSIX (copied on Windows), and mcpServers is mirrored from ~/.claude.json. --share-history also links projects/ and history.jsonl (POSIX only). POSIX uses os.execvpe; Windows keeps a thin wrapper that returns claude's exit code. Live sessions are detected from <config>/sessions/<pid>.json, with the procStart field guarding against reused pids. After exit, the rotated credential is copied back into the backup. --require-session refuses when N is already the default login. Only OAuth accounts are supported (API keys are refused).

features.name: map / unmap: directory-to-account mapping
features.how_it_works: <backup>/mappings.json maps a normalised absolute path (expanded, resolved, normcased) to an (email, organizationUuid) pair. A bare `cswap run` resolves the nearest mapped parent directory. Mappings are per machine and not exported.

features.name: Roster management
features.how_it_works: disable/enable sets a flag in sequence.json; disabled accounts are skipped by auto, by bare switch and by the best/next-available strategies, but can still be switched to explicitly. Also: alias N name / --unset; move A slot (moves or swaps slot numbers); swap A B; remove N; unclaimed [--purge ID]; purge (deletes all cswap data).

features.name: export / import
features.how_it_works: A plaintext JSON envelope (FORMAT_VERSION 1) with accounts[{number, email, credentials, config, ...}], written 0600 atomically; --account N exports one. By default it leaves out machine-shared MCP/plugin tokens and the device-bound trustedDeviceToken; --full includes all of ~/.claude.json and the whole credential object. Import skips existing accounts unless --force, validates email and slot number against path traversal, and replaces quarantined dead-token slots automatically. Encryption is left to the user (e.g. `cswap export - | gpg -c`). #164 documents refresh tokens revoked across machines when a pool of seats was shared between several installs.

features.name: config
features.how_it_works: <backup>/settings.json (schema 1), validated by `cswap config get/set/unset/path`. Keys: autoswitch.threshold (50-99.9), intervalSeconds (15-3600), cooldownSeconds, hysteresisPct, strategy (best, consume-first), includeApiKeyAccounts, unhealthyTicks, model (comma-separated names or 'all'); ui.theme (dark, light, auto).

features.name: TUI / watch
features.how_it_works: Textual app, opened by a bare `cswap` on a TTY, `cswap tui`, or `cswap watch` (straight to the live monitor). Keys: s switch, b best pick, w watch, g auto view (l live/dry-run, t or arrow keys for threshold), f refresh, ctrl+t theme. Switcher work runs in worker threads.

features.name: menubar and launchd service (macOS only)
features.how_it_works: Needs the rumps extra. Shows 5h, 7d and spend per account, switching, and optionally the auto engine in the background. --install-service writes ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.cswap.menubar.plist, which pins the console script, with logs in ~/Library/Logs/com.cswap.menubar.{log,err}.

features.name: upgrade / update check / migrations / logging
features.how_it_works: `cswap upgrade` detects a uv or pipx install. Update checks use https://pypi.org/pypi/claude-swap/json, cached for 24 h. Migrations run once: the legacy ~/.claude-swap-backup moves to $XDG_DATA_HOME/claude-swap, using a .migrating flag; Windows Credential Manager moves to files (CredWrite fails above 2,500 bytes, #45). The log is <backup>/claude-swap.log, and warning lines leave out emails. The tool refuses to run as root outside a container (detected via /.dockerenv, cgroup and overlay mountinfo).

features.name: NOT in main: Remote Control / Artifacts pin (PR #210, open)
features.how_it_works: An optional claude-swap[pin] extra delegating to the separate PyPI package cswap-pin. It is a local MITM HTTPS_PROXY that swaps the Authorization bearer only on /v1/code/sessions*, /v1/sessions/*, /api/frame/*, /v1/ultrareview/* and exactly /api/oauth/validate. It never touches /v1/messages or /api/oauth/token, and does not touch /v1/code/sessions/<id>/worker, which uses a per-session JWT. The proxy's CA is merged into NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS. Wiring goes into the env block of ~/.claude.json. Refused for Windows.

features.name: NOT in main: usage for setup-tokens and other proposals
features.how_it_works: PR #322 (open) runs one isolated `claude -p ok --output-format stream-json --verbose --model claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 --max-turns 1 --tools ""` under the profile and parses the last rate_limit_event. PR #229 (open) falls back to the anthropic-ratelimit-unified-* headers of a 1-token /v1/messages call when the endpoint returns 429. Other open proposals: #315/#308 warm-on-reset (a Haiku ping to start an idle account's 5h clock); #386/#387 `cswap run --auto`, per-session accounts that receive only an access token; #352 import-usage; #285 notifications; #176 statusline; #108 `cswap login` (a standalone PKCE browser OAuth flow); #90 service installs for auto (launchd/systemd/Task Scheduler).

credential_handling:
Storage:
- Active credential: what Claude Code itself reads. Linux, WSL and Windows use <CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR or ~/.claude>/.credentials.json, shaped {"claudeAiOauth":{accessToken, refreshToken, expiresAt(ms), refreshTokenExpiresAt(ms), scopes[]}, plus siblings mcpOAuth, pluginSecrets and trustedDeviceToken}. macOS uses the Keychain service 'Claude Code-credentials' (suffixed -<sha256(NFC raw CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR)[:8]> per config directory) through the `security` CLI, falling back to the file.
- Identity: oauthAccount in ~/.claude.json. Note the asymmetry: without CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR it is $HOME/.claude.json, not inside ~/.claude.
- Managed API keys: primaryApiKey in ~/.claude.json (or the Keychain item 'Claude Code'), plus customApiKeyResponses.approved holding key[-20:].
- Backups: base64 .enc files, NOT encrypted, mode 0600, under <backup>/credentials/. <backup> is ~/.claude-swap-backup on macOS and Windows, and ${XDG_DATA_HOME:-~/.local/share}/claude-swap on Linux and WSL. Superseded generations are kept as .enc.prev.

Copying and refreshing:
- A switch copies bytes between the backup and the live store while holding Claude Code's own locks (the mkdir-based .oauth_refresh.lock, ~/.claude.lock and ~/.claude.json.lock).
- Only inactive slots are refreshed (POST platform.claude.com/v1/oauth/token, client_id 9d1c250a-e61b-44d9-88ed-5944d1962f5e). A per-slot consume lock plus a fingerprint check makes sure a single-use refresh token is sent once.
- Before activation, a target is refreshed if its token expires within 10 minutes. A slot is quarantined on invalid_grant.
- Setup-tokens have no refresh token and no expiresAt, so none of the rotation machinery applies to them. cswap never refreshes them, and #382's reading of the Claude Code bundle says Claude Code treats such a credential as inference-only, never refreshes it and never logs out.

Documented risks of logging users out:
- /logout while adding accounts can revoke the stored refresh token (README, #189).
- Two copies of one refresh lineage (another machine, an export/import, a session profile plus the default login, or a background refresh on two machines) diverge. The first rotation revokes the other copy's access token immediately, observed as '401 OAuth access token has been revoked' or '403 OAuth token does not meet scope requirement … Please run /login' (#164, #381, #96).
- A switch that backs up a live store without OAuth over a slot's OAuth backup can destroy the refresh token (#383, #302, open).
- CLAUDE_SECURESTORAGE_CONFIG_DIR (Claude Code ≥2.1.220, which lets several config directories share one credential store) is handled only on capture. Consume and refresh refuse with 'store-unmirrored' (#293).

Meaning for Ashley: the ~/.ashley/accounts/<name> CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR layout plus CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN setup-tokens avoids every rotation hazard above. The one refresh-token credential Ashley holds, the claude.ai login used for remote-control, must never be copied into a second config directory or to another node.
limit_detection:
Mainline source: GET https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/usage.
- Headers: Bearer access token, anthropic-beta: oauth-2025-04-20, User-Agent claude-swap/1.0; 5 s timeout.
- Fields read: five_hour {utilization (percent 0-100), resets_at (ISO)}; seven_day {same}; extra_usage {is_enabled, used_credits (cents), monthly_limit (cents), utilization, currency, resets_at}.
- Per-model weekly windows come from limits[], with scope.model.display_name (e.g. 'Fable'), percent and resets_at.
- Headroom = 100 - max(5h, 7d, selected model windows). Auto-switch fires at 90% by default.
- Errors are classified as http-<code> (Retry-After parsed), timeout, network or bad-response.

Budget (measured by the author, see poll_policy.py): about 28-30 requests per rolling hour per identity; capacity only returns as requests age out, and in one regime the budget is per account, so a new token does not clear a block. Cadence is 180 s to 600 s, with an adaptive backoff after 429s.

Critical caveat for Ashley: a setup-token carries only user:inference, and /api/oauth/usage answers 403 for it on every pass. PR #322 reports that a handful of those 403s trip a host-wide 429 for an hour, which also blanks full-scope accounts on the same host. Mainline cswap therefore shows setup-token accounts as 'usage unavailable (http-403)' and never ranks or switches them.

Two working alternatives exist in unmerged PRs:
(a) rate_limit_event in `claude -p --output-format stream-json --verbose` output, as {"type":"rate_limit_event","rate_limit_info":{status, unifiedWindows:{five_hour:{utilization 0..1, resetsAt epoch s}, seven_day:{...}}}}. An exhausted account still emits it with status 'rejected' and utilization 1.0 and exits non-zero, so stdout should be parsed whatever the exit code. Verified by the PR author on Claude Code 2.1.257 and 2.1.260; not checked here against 2.1.283.
(b) The response headers of any /v1/messages call: anthropic-ratelimit-unified-status, -5h-utilization (fraction), -5h-reset (epoch s), -7d-utilization, -7d-reset and -representative-claim. These are also present on 429 responses but absent on 400/404, and carry no per-model or extra_usage data (#220, PR #229).

Ashley already runs every prompt as `claude -p`, so adding `--output-format stream-json --verbose` gives it (a) at no extra cost. That is the natural rotation trigger, with no polling and no 403s.

Other signals cswap uses: loginExpiresAt from refreshTokenExpiresAt, and the pace fields (expectedPct, aheadOfPace).
remote_control:
claude-swap has no remote or headless relay of its own; it is local-only. Headless-friendly pieces: add-token (a setup-token or API key read from stdin, with no browser and no API call); `auto --once --json` for cron or systemd timers, with exit codes 0, 1, 2 and 3 (JSON events); `list/status --json`; and the macOS launchd agent. The auto service installer (#90) and standalone PKCE login (PR #108) are unmerged.

Remote Control findings from contributor codeslake (#198, PR #210). These are measurements on 2.1.220-2.1.234, not verified here:
- A Remote Control session's owner is fixed by the bearer token that created it.
- If the account of the config directory running a bridge changes, the bridge drops with 'signed-in claude.ai account or organization changed on this machine — run /remote-control to reconnect'.
- The owner check compares accountUuid AND organizationUuid, via POST ${BASE_API_URL}/api/oauth/validate on reattach. Bridges persist bridgeOwnerAccountUuid and bridgeOwnerOrganizationUuid.
- /bridge (authenticated by OAuth) mints a per-session worker JWT that refreshes roughly every 8 h, used on /v1/code/sessions/<id>/worker.
- Artifacts (/api/frame/deploy/direct) are also owned by the publishing bearer.

Dead ends measured for splitting Remote Control from inference inside one session:
- CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN applies to both.
- An x-organization-uuid header is ignored.
- CLAUDE_BRIDGE_OAUTH_TOKEN is declared in the binary with no consumers.
- ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL disables /v1/code/sessions.
The only split that works is a MITM proxy (cswap-pin), still unmerged.

Meaning for Ashley: run `claude remote-control` under its own CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, with its own claude.ai login that rotation never writes to. Rotate only the worker config directories. Then a rotation can never trip the owner check and disconnect the phone.

Related: #296 asked cswap to expose session-profile paths for external launchers (withdrawn); PRs #386/#387 propose managed sessions that spread parallel workers across accounts.
platform_notes:
- **Linux / WSL:** credentials live in the plain file <config>/.credentials.json. Claude Code picks up a change on the next request through the mtime check. Backups go under ${XDG_DATA_HOME:-~/.local/share}/claude-swap, with a legacy migration from ~/.claude-swap-backup. Session mode symlinks shared items, and --share-history works.
- **Grid / HPC:** FileLock uses fcntl.flock, which gives no exclusion across nodes on NFS homes mounted local_lock=all (#372; fix PR #374, unmerged). Claude Code's own locks are mkdir-based and safe across nodes. Live-session detection is node-local (pid, /proc/<pid>/stat procStart), so a shared home seen from several nodes will misjudge liveness. For Ashley on shared Panasas or CephFS: use mkdir locks, keep each account's config directory used by one node at a time, and put IPC under /dev/shm as the project already does.
- **Windows:** file-based backups; Credential Manager was dropped because CredWrite fails above 2,500 bytes (#45). Session mode copies instead of symlinking, and --share-history is unsupported (a junction proposal is #292). `cswap run` stays resident as a subprocess wrapper instead of exec. It uses truststore for OS TLS trust, which fixed refreshes on Windows (PR #78), and forces UTF-8 output for cp1252 consoles.
- **macOS:** Keychain through the `security` CLI (service 'Claude Code-credentials', per-directory hash suffix), with a Keychain cache of about 30 s. It falls back to a file when the Keychain is locked or unavailable (headless/SSH), and re-probes after a 60 s cooldown. Open ACL bugs #279 and #373. The menu bar (rumps) and the launchd agent are macOS-only.
- **All platforms:** requires Python ≥3.12, and refuses to run as root outside a detected container. Container detection looks at the CONTAINER env var, /.dockerenv, and docker/lxc/containerd/kubepods in /proc/1/cgroup or overlay in mountinfo. Apptainer is not explicitly detected.

Local clones used for reading: C:\Users\grego\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\c--Users-grego-OneDrive-Desktop-CTSpinoPelvic1K-1\0599380b-0d32-4e19-b5be-65bdd1017566\scratchpad\cswap-desktop and ...\scratchpad\claude-swap (upstream, v0.27.0b1, for the mechanisms the desktop app delegates to)
what_it_is: "Claude Swap" is an Electron desktop app (Electron 44, React 19, Tailwind 4, electron-vite, electron-updater 6.8.9) by Purwa Sabrang Ramadhan. It is a graphical front end for realiti4/claude-swap (`cswap`), a Python CLI that manages several Claude Code logins and switches between them. The app is a thin client. It does not bundle Python or cswap, never writes credentials and never calls Anthropic. Every read and write is a subprocess call to the installed `cswap` binary with `--json` (schema v1), parsed in the Electron main process and pushed to the renderer over IPC. The app reads only four things directly: cswap's `mappings.json`, a file watcher on cswap's vault directory, two non-secret fields from Claude Code's `.credentials.json` (for a plan badge), and GitHub release metadata for its own updates. Main code: `src/main` (driver, auto-switch runner, vault watcher, tray, updater, IPC), `src/preload` (`window.cswap` via contextBridge), `src/renderer` (UI, which also runs in a plain browser against a mock API), and `test/fake-cswap` (a stand-in CLI with the same verbs, JSON and stdin prompts). The fake reports cswap 0.25.0; upstream `pyproject.toml` is now 0.27.0b1. The app has no ownership model: any email, org, setup-token or API key can be added, so the tool itself does nothing to enforce Ashley's one-person, one-account policy.

features.name: CLI driver (every operation goes through cswap)
features.how_it_works: `CswapDriver.run(args,{stdin,timeoutMs,cwd})` spawns the binary with `windowsHide`. It uses `shell:true` with manual quoting only when the binary is a Windows `.cmd`/`.bat` shim. Environment: `NO_COLOR=1`, `PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8`, `PYTHONUTF8=1`, `CLAUDE_SWAP_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1`. Default timeout is 60 s (120 s for list/switch, 180 s for `auto --once`, 300 s for upgrade). On timeout, `killTree` runs `taskkill /pid N /t /f` on Windows, because killing the .cmd shell leaves the python grandchild holding stdout; elsewhere it uses child.kill. JSON parsing takes stdout from the first `{`. A top-level `{error:{type,message}}` envelope becomes `{ok:false,error}`; otherwise a nonzero exit becomes CliError with stderr text. All mutations go through `serial()`, a promise-chain queue, so two clicks never race inside cswap's own locks. Every mutation is followed by `core.afterMutation()`, which triggers a refresh.

features.name: Accounts table: 5-hour, 7-day and per-model usage with reset countdowns
features.how_it_works: Runs `cswap list --json` and receives `{schemaVersion, activeAccountNumber, accounts[]}`. Each account carries `number, email, organizationName/Uuid, isOrganization, active, usageStatus, usage{fiveHour, sevenDay, scoped[{name,...}]}, alias, disabled, usageFetchedAt, usageAgeSeconds, lastGoodUsage, lastGoodFetchedAt`. Each window has `pct, resetsAt, countdown, clock`. Per-model weekly windows (`scoped`, e.g. 'Fable') get their own table columns, collected across all accounts in first-seen order. When live usage is missing, `lastGoodUsage` is shown, and a reset time already in the past reads 'reset passed'. Colour: 100% or more is danger, 80% or more is warn. The 'binding' window is whichever of 5h, 7d or scoped has the highest pct. Status chips map `usageStatus` values ok, token_expired, api_key, keychain_unavailable, relogin_required, foreign_credential, no_credentials and unavailable to labels. Usage can be shown as bars or rings (`UsageRing.tsx`). Below 780 px of width each row becomes a card.

features.name: Pace marker on weekly windows
features.how_it_works: cswap adds `expectedPct`, `aheadOfPace`, `projectedExhaustionAt` and `willLastToReset` to weekly windows once the week is about a day old. It computes these itself (upstream `pace.py`); the app only renders them. The app draws a notch at `expectedPct` on the bar or ring, shows an 'ahead' chip, and uses tooltip text such as 'spread evenly you'd be at ~X% by now' and 'at this rate it runs out before the reset'. The `showPace` setting toggles it.

features.name: Subscription/plan badge (Pro / Max 5x / Max 20x / Team · Max 20x)
features.how_it_works: `readActivePlan()` opens `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/.credentials.json`, or `~/.claude/.credentials.json` when that variable is unset. It reads only `claudeAiOauth.subscriptionType` and `claudeAiOauth.rateLimitTier`, and no token is assigned to a variable. `labelFor()` uses subscriptionType as the plan and takes only the plan word and the `(\d+)x` multiplier from the tier; a tier that names a different plan gives 'Team · Max 20x'. This works only for the currently live account, because other accounts' copies are inside the cswap vault. After each refresh, `PlanStore.observe(activeEmail)` records the label per email in `<userData>/plans.json` (tmp file, then rename), so badges survive a switch. On macOS the credentials are in the Keychain, so no badge appears. Ashley relevance: a setup-token passed in `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` leaves no `.credentials.json`, so this route gives Ashley workers no plan information.

features.name: One-click switch and rotation
features.how_it_works: Switching runs `cswap switch <slot|email|alias> --json [--force]`. Rotation runs `cswap switch --json [--strategy best|next-available]`; with no strategy cswap uses its own rotation order. The result is a SwitchPayload `{switched, from, to, strategy, reason, message, warnings[], models?, modelSource?}`, and warnings are shown as a toast. The UI never passes `--force`, which per the import dialog text bypasses the backup of the current login. Switching is available from row buttons, the rotate menu (Next / Best (most quota left) / Next available (skip limited)), the tray menu and the Ctrl+K palette.

features.name: Add account from the current Claude Code login
features.how_it_works: Runs `cswap add [--slot N] [--alias A]`. When the slot is taken, cswap asks 'Overwrite slot N? [y/N]', and the driver pre-writes `y\n` or `n\n` to stdin depending on an Overwrite switch in the UI. The dialog tells the user to run `claude`, then `/login`, and warns: 'Do not run /logout on the account you are leaving — Claude Code may revoke the token cswap stored for it.' Re-adding an already-managed email refreshes its stored credentials rather than duplicating it. The row menu also offers 'Re-add from the current login' to refresh one slot.

features.name: Add from a setup-token or API key (secret passed on stdin)
features.how_it_works: Runs `cswap add-token - [--email E] [--slot N]` with stdin `<token>\n<y|n>\n`. The token never appears in argv, stdin is never logged, and the app does not keep the token. The UI detects the type from the prefix: `sk-ant-oat` is a setup-token, `sk-ant-api` an API key. Upstream (`switcher.py`) wraps a setup-token as `{"claudeAiOauth":{"accessToken":T,"scopes":["user:inference"]}}` with placeholder identity `setup-token-{slot}@token.local` and no org metadata, and makes no Anthropic call. Ashley relevance: this is the same token type Ashley already uses.

features.name: Remove, disable/enable, alias, move, swap
features.how_it_works: Remove runs `cswap remove <t>` with stdin `y\n`, after the UI makes the user type the slot number or email. The UI says Claude Code is not logged out and the live login stays until a switch or /logout. `cswap disable|enable <t>` holds an account out of rotation. `cswap alias <t> <name>` or `--unset` sets or clears an alias (letters, digits, `. - _`, not purely numeric). `cswap move <t> <slot>` and `cswap swap <a> <b>` reorder slots; aliases, backups and session history move with the account.

features.name: Auto-switch runner (long-lived child process with a JSONL event stream)
features.how_it_works: `AutoSwitchRunner.start()` spawns `cswap auto --json [--dry-run]` with `PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1`; only one runs at a time. stdout is split on newlines and each line parsed as an AutoEvent `{schemaVersion, event, ts, ...}`. Unparseable lines become `raw` and stderr becomes `stderr` events; the last 500 are kept in a ring buffer. Event kinds: `poll` (active, `windowsPct{slot:{'5h','7d',model}}`, `headroomPct{slot}`, `threshold`), `switch` (trigger e.g. 'at-limit', from, to, warnings, dryRun), `no-switch` (reason, detail), `account-quarantined` / `account-unquarantined` (number, email, reason), `all-exhausted` (earliestResetAt), `sleep` (seconds, until), `error`, `config-warning`. The events switch, quarantined and all-exhausted trigger a list refresh. A `switch` event shows an Electron Notification ('cswap switched account' or 'would switch (dry run)') when notifyOnAutoSwitch is on. Stop sends SIGTERM on POSIX and `taskkill /t /f` on Windows, with SIGKILL after 5 s. The runner can start with the app (`autoStartAutoSwitch`) and be toggled from the tray. It is a child of the GUI, so quitting the app stops it (`dispose`).

features.name: 'Check now' (a single auto-switch tick)
features.how_it_works: Runs `cswap auto --once --json [--dry-run]` through the serial queue. Exit codes map to outcomes: 0 switched, 1 error, 2 no action (below threshold), 3 blocked (wanted to switch but no viable target). JSONL events in stdout are merged into the feed. Ashley relevance: this exit-code contract fits cron or Slurm-style supervision well.

features.name: Editor for cswap's own auto-switch settings
features.how_it_works: Reads `cswap config list --json`, which returns `{path, settings:[{key,value,isSet}]}`. Changes run `cswap config set <k> <v>`; reset runs `cswap config unset <k>`. Keys exposed: `autoswitch.threshold` (50–99.9, switch when the binding 5h/7d window reaches it), `autoswitch.intervalSeconds` (15–3600), `autoswitch.cooldownSeconds` (minimum time between proactive switches), `autoswitch.hysteresisPct` (a target must beat the active account by this much), `autoswitch.strategy` ('best' = most quota left, 'consume-first' = burn the soonest-resetting weekly window first), `autoswitch.model` (also switch on per-model weekly limits, e.g. 'Fable', 'Fable,Opus' or 'all'), `autoswitch.unhealthyTicks` (consecutive failed polls before an account is unhealthy), and `autoswitch.includeApiKeyAccounts`. Defaults seen only in the fake CLI: 90, 60, 300, 10, best, '', 3, false. Changes take effect on the next auto-switch start. `cswap config path` also locates the vault.

features.name: Session mode (one terminal runs as a stored account)
features.how_it_works: `launchSession(bin, target, cwd)` opens a new terminal running `<cswap> run <slot>` in a chosen directory (a mapped project, else home). Windows: `cmd.exe /d /s /k "title ...& \"bin\" run N"` with `detached` and `windowsVerbatimArguments`. macOS: osascript tells Terminal.app to `do script "cd ... && bin run N"`. Linux: tries x-terminal-emulator, gnome-terminal, konsole, then xterm with `bash -lc '...; exec $SHELL'`. Upstream (`session.py`), `cswap run` sets `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=<vault>/sessions/<num>-<email-slug>/` seeded with a plaintext `.credentials.json`. It shares settings.json, keybindings.json, CLAUDE.md, skills/, commands/ and agents/ (symlinks on POSIX, re-synced copies on Windows); `--share-history` also links projects/ and history.jsonl. It then execs claude (a subprocess on Windows). The default `~/.claude` login and other terminals are untouched. Ashley relevance: this is the same per-account `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` isolation Ashley uses under `~/.ashley/accounts/<name>`.

features.name: Directory mappings (a project folder tied to an account)
features.how_it_works: Reads `<vault>/mappings.json` directly, accepting either `{mappings:{path:{email,organizationUuid}}}` or a flat map, and joins it to accounts by email and org. When the file is absent it falls back to parsing the text output of `cswap map` (lines like `<path> → 2: me@x [tag]`; ANSI stripped), because that command has no --json. Adding runs `cswap map <t> <path>` (folder picker); removing runs `cswap unmap <path>`. Each row can open a session-mode terminal in that folder.

features.name: Token diagnostics
features.how_it_works: Runs `cswap list --token-status`, a plain-text report of where each account's OAuth token comes from and whether it is still valid. It is shown ANSI-stripped in a dialog.

features.name: Export/import of .cswap backups
features.how_it_works: Export runs `cswap export <file> [--account N] [--full]` to a path from a save dialog (default `claude-swap-YYYY-MM-DD.cswap`). The UI warns the file is plaintext JSON containing login credentials. Without `--full`, machine-shared MCP/plugin OAuth tokens stay on the machine. Import runs `cswap import <file> [--force]`. Per the UI text, existing accounts are skipped except slots whose refresh token has died, which are replaced automatically, and a stale export can carry an already-superseded token.

features.name: Unclaimed credential entries
features.how_it_works: `cswap unclaimed` lists stashed credentials that cswap cannot attribute to a slot; the text is parsed as `<id> slot <n> <reason>`. `cswap unclaimed --purge <id>` deletes one. Shown under Settings → Data.

features.name: Vault watcher (sync with terminal and TUI changes)
features.how_it_works: The vault root is `dirname(cswap config path)`. Defaults: `$XDG_DATA_HOME/claude-swap` or `~/.local/share/claude-swap` on Linux, `~/.claude-swap-backup` elsewhere. An `fs.watch` (non-persistent) on that directory ignores everything except sequence.json, settings.json, mappings.json and autoswitch_state.json. After a 600 ms debounce it triggers `refresh()`, so a switch made in a terminal appears within about a second. Ashley relevance: the same cheap sync could be done by watching `~/.ashley/accounts`.

features.name: Refresh scheduling
features.how_it_works: Refreshes every `refreshSeconds` (default 60, floor 15, 0 = never), on window focus or show at most once per 10 s, on vault change, and after every mutation. Concurrent refreshes share one in-flight promise. The Settings hint notes that cswap throttles its own calls to Anthropic, so this setting only controls how often the list is re-read.

features.name: Locating, installing and upgrading cswap
features.how_it_works: Resolution order: Settings path, then the `CSWAP_DESKTOP_BIN` env var, then candidate paths (`~/.local/bin/cswap[.exe]`, `%APPDATA%\Python\Scripts`, `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Python\Scripts`, `/opt/homebrew/bin`, `/usr/local/bin`, `~/.pipx/bin`), then PATH. On macOS it also asks the login shell (`$SHELL -ilc 'echo -n "$PATH"'`), because Finder-launched apps miss the shell PATH. Each candidate is validated with `--version`. The onboarding screen can run `uv tool install claude-swap` (uv found in ~/.local/bin, ~/.cargo/bin, homebrew or PATH). Settings offers `cswap upgrade`. cswap is deliberately not bundled: per the README, 'two cswap versions writing the same vault is how accounts go missing'.

features.name: Command log
features.how_it_works: Every CLI call is recorded as `{id, at, args, exitCode, durationMs, ok, stdout, stderr, error}`, with stdout and stderr each capped at 20,000 characters. The log is an in-memory ring of 300 entries pushed live to a Log page. Arguments are not redacted because secrets never go in argv; stdin is never recorded.

features.name: System tray
features.how_it_works: The tooltip shows the active account and 5h/7d percentages. The menu lists every account ('● N. alias · email — 5h x% · 7d y%'; click to switch), plus Rotate to next, Switch to best, Refresh usage, Start/Stop auto-switch and Quit. The menu rebuilds on 'accounts' and 'autoStatus' events. Close-to-tray and start-minimized are options. Launch at login uses `app.setLoginItemSettings({openAtLogin, args:['--hidden']})` in packaged builds. A single-instance lock applies.

features.name: Privacy mask
features.how_it_works: One toggle (`maskEmails`) keeps the first three characters of each email local part and replaces the rest with bullets. Organisation names are masked the same way. Names of the form '<email>'s Organization' are treated as personal accounts and labelled 'personal', not as an org.

features.name: Command palette and keyboard shortcuts
features.how_it_works: Ctrl/Cmd+K opens the palette, which filters accounts by email, alias, exact slot number or organisation name, plus page names, and switches on Enter. Ctrl+R refreshes and Ctrl+, opens Settings.

features.name: Self-update
features.how_it_works: Uses electron-updater against GitHub releases (`latest.yml`), loaded with createRequire because `import()` inside the asar failed silently. The app checks 15 s after start and every 6 h, downloads in the background and installs on quit. 'Restart & install' calls `quitAndInstall(true,true)` (silent NSIS). Code-signature verification is stubbed out because builds are unsigned. The log goes to `<userData>/updater.log`. macOS and unpackaged builds are disabled; there a manual check reads `api.github.com/repos/TheSkinnyRat/cswap-desktop/releases/latest` and links to the release.

features.name: App settings store
features.how_it_works: `<appData>/cswap-desktop/settings.json` (path pinned so renaming the product does not orphan it; `CSWAP_DESKTOP_USERDATA` overrides) is written atomically via tmp + rename. Keys: cswapPath, theme (light/dark/system), refreshSeconds, closeToTray, startMinimized, launchAtLogin, notifyOnAutoSwitch, autoStartAutoSwitch, autoDryRun, autoUpdate, maskEmails, refreshOnFocus, usageView (bars/rings), showPace, sidebarCollapsed.

features.name: Test seams
features.how_it_works: `test/fake-cswap/fake-cswap.mjs` implements every verb, the JSON schema, the stdin prompts and the auto JSONL loop, backed by `FAKE_CSWAP_STATE`; `FAKE_CSWAP_FAIL=<verb>` forces an error envelope. `CSWAP_DESKTOP_TEST_DIALOGS` stubs native dialogs and `CSWAP_DESKTOP_TEST_NO_SPAWN` suppresses terminal spawns. Opt-in real e2e tests: `CSWAP_REAL=1` is read-only, `CSWAP_REAL_SWITCH=<slot>` does one real switch and back while checking `cswap status --json`, and `CSWAP_REAL_RUN=<slot>` opens one real session terminal. CI runs typecheck, vitest and Playwright on Ubuntu (Xvfb) and Windows. Tagging `v*` triggers electron-builder for Windows (NSIS and portable), Linux (AppImage and deb) and macOS (dmg for x64 and arm64), all unsigned.

features.name: Left out on purpose: purge
features.how_it_works: `cswap purge`, which deletes every account, has no UI; the README says to use the CLI for it.

credential_handling:
cswap-desktop has no credential store of its own. It does not copy, rotate or refresh tokens; all of that is cswap's. Its direct contact with credentials:
(1) plan.ts reads `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/.credentials.json`, or `~/.claude/.credentials.json`, for the live account only, and extracts only `claudeAiOauth.subscriptionType` and `rateLimitTier`. It caches a label per email in `<userData>/plans.json`.
(2) add-token passes the secret on stdin (`cswap add-token -`, then the y/n overwrite answer), never in argv, and never logs it. The in-memory command log keeps args plus stdout/stderr (up to 20,000 characters each, last 300 calls, not written to disk).
(3) Export writes plaintext JSON with credentials; the UI warns about this. `--full` adds machine-shared MCP/plugin OAuth tokens.

What cswap does underneath, read from upstream claude-swap source:
- Refresh posts to https://platform.claude.com/v1/oauth/token with client_id 9d1c250a-e61b-44d9-88ed-5944d1962f5e (`oauth.py`).
- Stored per-account backups on Linux, WSL and Windows are base64 `.enc` files at mode 0600 under the vault's credentials dir (`credentials.py` `_atomic_b64_write`); on macOS they go in the Keychain. The desktop's plan.ts comment calls these copies 'encrypted', but the upstream code only base64-encodes them. On a shared grid filesystem, file permissions are the only protection.
- Setup-tokens are stored as `{claudeAiOauth:{accessToken, scopes:['user:inference']}}`. Upstream notes they are inference-only server-side and that wider scopes cause 403s on profile endpoints.
- Session mode seeds a plaintext `.credentials.json` into `<vault>/sessions/<num>-<slug>/` and points `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` there. On macOS, Claude hashes that path into its keychain service name, so each profile gets its own keychain entry.

Logout and broken-refresh risks the app spells out:
- 'Do not run /logout on the account you are leaving — Claude Code may revoke the token cswap stored for it.'
- Removing an account from cswap does not log Claude Code out.
- A stale export can carry an already-superseded token, meaning a rotated refresh token; on import, slots whose refresh token has died are replaced automatically.
- `switch --force` activates stored credentials without backing up the current login. The UI never passes it.
- Two cswap installs writing one vault 'is how accounts go missing', so the app refuses to bundle cswap and queues all mutations.

For Ashley: keep exactly one writer per credential store. The node-side worker and the VS Code extension must not both mutate `~/.ashley/accounts`. Treat `/logout` on the node, including in the separate claude.ai login used for remote-control, as able to revoke tokens.
limit_detection:
The desktop app does not detect limits itself; it renders what cswap reports.

Passive detection: `cswap list --json`. Per account it gives `usageStatus` (ok, token_expired, api_key, keychain_unavailable, relogin_required, foreign_credential, no_credentials, unavailable) and `usage.fiveHour`, `usage.sevenDay` and `usage.scoped[]` (per-model weekly limits, e.g. name 'Fable'). Each window has `pct, resetsAt, countdown, clock`; weekly windows add `expectedPct, aheadOfPace, projectedExhaustionAt, willLastToReset`. Freshness comes from `usageFetchedAt`/`usageAgeSeconds`, and the last successful reading is kept as `lastGoodUsage`/`lastGoodFetchedAt`. The UI colours 80% or more as warn and 100% or more as danger, and picks the 'binding' window as the maximum pct across 5h, 7d and scoped.

Active detection: `cswap auto --json` emits JSONL.
- `poll` carries `windowsPct{slot:{'5h','7d',<model>}}`, `headroomPct{slot}` and `threshold`.
- `switch` carries trigger (e.g. 'at-limit'), from, to, warnings and dryRun.
- `all-exhausted` carries `earliestResetAt`.
- `account-quarantined` and `account-unquarantined` mark accounts taken out of or returned to rotation.
- `auto --once` exits 0 when it switched, 1 on error, 2 when below threshold and 3 when blocked.
- Tunables: `autoswitch.threshold` (50–99.9), intervalSeconds, cooldownSeconds, hysteresisPct, strategy (best or consume-first), model (per-model limits), unhealthyTicks and includeApiKeyAccounts.

Upstream source of the numbers: GET https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/usage with `Authorization: Bearer <access token>` and `anthropic-beta: oauth-2025-04-20` (`oauth.py` `request_usage_data`). `poll_policy.py` records a measured budget of about 28–30 requests per trailing ~60-minute window per identity. It is not a refill bucket: a burst blocks that identity for up to an hour. The identity is sometimes the account or org and sometimes the token, and re-authenticating cannot be relied on to clear a block.

Unknown: whether the usage endpoint answers for a setup-token (scope `user:inference` only). Neither repo shows it working; the desktop's fake CLI returns usage for setup-token accounts, but it is a fake. Ashley workers authenticate with `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` setup-tokens and have no `.credentials.json`, so this polling route, and the plan badge, may not be available. Ashley may still have to detect limits from `claude -p` errors, and that is not addressed in either repo.
remote_control:
There is nothing about `claude remote-control`, claude.ai or phone access, sessions on other machines, a network relay, or headless operation. The app is a local Electron GUI.
- `--hidden` only starts it with the window hidden in the tray.
- The auto-switch loop is a child process of the GUI and stops when the app quits.
- Accounts move between machines only through the plaintext `.cswap` export and import files.
- 'Session mode' opens a local terminal with a per-account `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`.

What does transfer to Ashley's grid-plus-relay design is the underlying CLI. cswap is a Python tool that runs headless on Linux, with its vault at `$XDG_DATA_HOME/claude-swap`. Its README recommends `add-token` 'on headless servers', and it exposes machine-readable contracts: `list --json`, `switch --json`, the `auto --json` JSONL stream, `auto --once` exit codes, and `config list/set/unset --json`. An Ashley worker could run `cswap auto --json` inside the Slurm job and forward its JSONL through the existing relay to the VS Code extension. The extension would render it the way `Auto.tsx` does, and could reuse `describe()`, which formats each event kind. The one caveat is that cswap's switch strategies assume several distinct logins. Under the one-person, one-account policy, Ashley would need its own guard, because setup-token accounts carry only placeholder emails (`setup-token-N@token.local`) and no org, so cswap's data cannot confirm who owns a credential.
platform_notes:
Windows:
- cswap is usually a `.cmd` shim or `cswap.exe`. The driver switches to `shell:true` with manual quoting only for .cmd/.bat.
- Timeouts and auto-switch stop use `taskkill /pid N /t /f`, because Windows has no SIGTERM and killing the shell leaves the Python grandchild alive.
- The session terminal is `cmd.exe /d /s /k` with `windowsVerbatimArguments`, because Node's backslash-escaped quotes break cmd.
- Candidate binary paths include `%APPDATA%\\Python\\Scripts` and `%LOCALAPPDATA%\\Programs\\Python\\Scripts`. The vault is `~/.claude-swap-backup`.
- Packaged as NSIS and portable exe, unsigned (SmartScreen prompt). Auto-updates silently.
- Upstream cswap stores backups as base64 `.enc` files and re-syncs copies (not symlinks) into session profiles, so `--share-history` is POSIX-only.

macOS:
- Credentials live in the Keychain, so there is no plan badge.
- The login-shell PATH is fetched because Finder launches with a short PATH.
- Session terminal via osascript and Terminal.app.
- Unsigned dmg, so no auto-update; it links to the release instead.
- Upstream, each `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` hashes to its own keychain entry.

Linux:
- The vault is `$XDG_DATA_HOME/claude-swap`, default `~/.local/share/claude-swap`.
- The terminal fallback chain is x-terminal-emulator, gnome-terminal, konsole, then xterm, each via `bash -lc`.
- Ships as AppImage and deb; CI runs e2e under Xvfb.
- Upstream uses a plaintext `.credentials.json` as the only credential mechanism, with base64 `.enc` backups at 0600.

WSL: nothing specific in the desktop repo. Upstream groups WSL with Linux (base64 `.enc` backups).
